variants.title: Payment API delays checkout
variants.context: The checkout endpoint calls a payment provider synchronously and waits on every call.
variants.constraint: The dependency is slow and thread-blocking.
variants.question: What makes request latency recover?
variants.expectedPattern: Enqueue the payment work and return quickly to the user.
wrongChoices: Move the API code into the browser

variants.title: Email sends hang the request path
variants.context: Emails are sent during signup and each request waits for SMTP completion.
variants.constraint: External email sending is slow and often unreliable.
variants.question: What should happen after the user account is created?
variants.expectedPattern: Persist a work item and process it asynchronously.

variants.title: Thumbnails generate too slowly
variants.context: Users upload photos and the app renders thumbnails inline in the request path.
variants.constraint: Thumbnail generation is slow and deferrable.
variants.question: What is the correct design?
variants.expectedPattern: Store the upload, enqueue the thumbnail job, and respond immediately.
wrongChoices: Render thumbnails in the request thread
Cache the upload in the browser
Queue thumbnails without storing the original

variants.title: Pay later crash
variants.context: A worker crashes after charging a card but before acknowledging the message.
variants.constraint: The queue may redeliver the same job.
variants.question: How do you avoid charging twice?
variants.expectedPattern: Use idempotency keys and a safe deduplication strategy.
wrongChoices: Let the request handle the charge

variants.title: Flash sale on the checkout system
variants.context: Payment, email, and order processing happen inside the request while the sale peaks.
variants.constraint: Downstream dependencies are slow and the pool is exhausting threads.
variants.question: What is the right architectural move?
variants.expectedPattern: Queue the expensive downstream tasks and make the request path short.

variants.title: Background workers back up
variants.context: The queue is growing and workers are falling behind under a sudden spike.
variants.constraint: Work is queueing faster than it can be processed.
variants.question: What should be added to prevent collapse?
variants.expectedPattern: Backpressure, retry policies, worker parallelism, and workload prioritization.

variants.title: Complex order processing
variants.context: After a user places an order, the platform calculates taxes, emits notifications, and updates a ledger.
variants.constraint: These steps do not need to complete before the user receives confirmation.
variants.question: How should the order flow be modeled?
variants.expectedPattern: Acknowledge the order quickly, then process the downstream work asynchronously.
wrongChoices: All work on the web request

variants.title: Queue message duplication
variants.context: A message is processed twice because a worker crashes before acknowledging it.
variants.constraint: At-least-once delivery is expected.
variants.question: What safety property must the job handler provide?
variants.expectedPattern: Idempotent processing so duplicate messages do not cause duplicate side effects.

variants.title: User places order but waits too long
variants.context: The order request waits for analytics, tax calculation, and three downstream APIs before returning a response.
variants.constraint: Only the order status is needed immediately.
variants.question: How do you improve user experience without losing correctness?
variants.expectedPattern: Queue non-critical follow-up work and acknowledge the order quickly.
wrongChoices: Wait for all APIs in the request

variants.title: Crashes during message processing
variants.context: A worker starts processing a message, fails mid-way, and the queue redelivers it.
variants.constraint: The side effect is not safe to repeat unless designed carefully.
variants.question: What must you design for?
variants.expectedPattern: Idempotent handlers, retry limits, and observational state.

variants.title: Webhook fan-out blocks the API
variants.context: A billing service calls 12 partner webhooks inside the same HTTP handler.
variants.constraint: Partners are slow and sometimes unreachable.
variants.question: How do you isolate partner latency?
variants.expectedPattern: Persist the event, enqueue outbound webhooks, and retry each partner independently.
wrongChoices: Wait for every partner before returning 200
Drop webhooks when a partner is slow

variants.title: Poison message stalls the queue
variants.context: One malformed payload crashes every worker that touches it, so the queue never drains.
variants.constraint: Later valid jobs are stuck behind the bad one.
variants.question: What failure-handling pattern unblocks the line?
variants.expectedPattern: After limited retries, move the poison message to a dead-letter queue and keep consuming.
wrongChoices: Retry the same message forever on the main queue
Stop all workers until a human notices

variants.title: Visibility timeout too short
variants.context: Video transcodes take 8 minutes, but the message becomes visible again after 30 seconds.
variants.constraint: Multiple workers start the same job.
variants.question: What queue setting must match the work?
variants.expectedPattern: Set visibility timeout (or heartbeat extend) longer than the real processing time.
wrongChoices: Process transcodes on the web request

variants.title: Signup SMS in the request
variants.context: Phone verification SMS is sent synchronously and the carrier API times out at peak.
variants.constraint: Account creation can succeed without waiting on SMS.
variants.question: What should the API do on signup?
variants.expectedPattern: Create the user, enqueue the SMS job, and return; workers send and retry the message.
wrongChoices: Fail signup if SMS is slow
Increase the HTTP timeout to 2 minutes
Send SMS from a database trigger only

variants.title: Retry storm after an outage
variants.context: A downstream API recovers and every delayed job retries at once.
variants.constraint: The dependency cannot absorb a synchronized burst.
variants.question: How do you retry safely?
variants.expectedPattern: Exponential backoff with jitter and a retry budget so jobs do not stampede.
wrongChoices: Retry all jobs immediately with no delay

variants.title: Exactly-once assumed on Kafka
variants.context: A consumer increments a coupon-used counter on every message and the counter doubles after rebalance.
variants.constraint: The broker delivers at least once.
variants.question: What must the consumer implement?
variants.expectedPattern: Idempotent updates keyed by message or coupon id so redelivery does not double-count.
wrongChoices: Assume Kafka is exactly-once for side effects

variants.title: Priority work stuck behind bulk import
variants.context: Password-reset emails sit behind a 2-million-row CSV import on one queue.
variants.constraint: User-facing jobs cannot wait on bulk work.
variants.question: How should work be separated?
variants.expectedPattern: Use priority queues or separate worker pools for interactive versus bulk jobs.
wrongChoices: One FIFO queue for every job type
Run imports on the API process

variants.title: Outbox missing after a crash
variants.context: The API writes an order row, then crashes before publishing to the queue, so fulfillment never starts.
variants.constraint: The database write committed; the message did not.
variants.question: What pattern keeps state and messages aligned?
variants.expectedPattern: Transactional outbox: write the event in the same transaction, then a relay publishes it.
wrongChoices: Publish first and write the order later without a transaction
Rely on the user to click again

variants.title: Unbounded queue memory
variants.context: Producers keep enqueueing during a worker outage until the broker runs out of disk.
variants.constraint: Consumers are down for hours.
variants.question: What protects the system?
variants.expectedPattern: Backpressure, retention limits, and producer throttling when the queue cannot drain.
wrongChoices: Infinite retention and no producer limits
Drop the broker and keep producing to /dev/null

variants.title: Long saga without compensation
variants.context: Booking reserves a flight, then hotel reservation fails, but the flight stay reserved.
variants.constraint: Steps are async and can fail independently.
variants.question: What failure handling is missing?
variants.expectedPattern: A saga with compensating actions (or a state machine) to undo completed steps on later failure.
wrongChoices: A single distributed transaction across all vendors
Retry only the hotel forever without releasing the flight
